 SMT PUSHPALATHA M.K., SR PP  THIS CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 10.06.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:40479 Crl.Rev.Pet.No.90 of 2025  -3-  G. GIRISH, J.
The order dated 21.11.2024 of the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Manjeri, in Crl.M.P.No.4959 of 2024 in C.C.No.326 of 2017 is under challenge in this revision petition.
The aforesaid petition was filed by the petitioners herein, who are accused Nos.2 to 7 in that case for discharge under Section 239 Cr.P.C.

The allegations against the petitioners is that they perpetrated matrimonial cruelty envisaged under Section 498A IPC upon the defacto complainant, in addition to criminal breach of trust envisaged under Section 406 IPC, by misappropriating the gold ornaments and money of the Joshitha.T vs State Of Kerala Represented By The ... on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127147373/
2 defacto complainant.
2.

The learned Magistrate, by the impugned order, found that there are sufficient grounds to proceed against the petitioners for the commission of the offences under Sections 498A and 406 IPC read with Section 34 IPC.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

4. On going through the First Information Statement of the defacto complainant, it is seen that there is only a vague allegation as against the 1st petitioner herein, who is the 2nd accused in the crime.

Apart from a bald contention that the 1st petitioner received some gold ornaments from the defacto complainant and failed to return it, there is absolutely nothing to connect the 1st petitioner with the offence alleged in the crime.
However, as against the other petitioners, the defacto complainant has got definite and precise allegations which would amount to physical and mental cruelty envisaged under Section 498A IPC.
Therefore, the learned Magistrate cannot be found at fault for disallowing the prayer to discharge by petitioners 2 to 6, who are accused Nos.3 to 7.

Hence,
the impugned order is liable to be interfered to the limited extent, wherein the prayer for quashing the proceedings against the 1st petitioner was declined.

In the result, the petition stands allowed in part as follows :-
2025:KER:40479 (i) The proceedings against the 1st revision petitioner, who is the 2nd accused in C.C.No.326 of 2017 on the files of the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Manjeri, stand quashed.

(ii) It is made clear that there is absolutely no legal impediment for the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate to proceed with the trial against petitioners 2 to 6, who are accused Nos.3 to 7 in the Final Report.

Sd/-
